StrainChain's METRC sync doesn't just log a transfer manifest — it pulls Michigan's seed-to-sale API directly, with retry and fallback built in, so a distributor's compliance record isn't a spreadsheet somebody re-keys after the fact.

Every batch also gets its own event ledger: cultivated, harvested, lab-tested, packaged, transferred, received at the dispensary. Each stage is a separate record, not a checkbox — so a regulator or a buyer can trace a batch through the stages it actually passed, in order, instead of trusting a single end-of-chain attestation.

Batch registration hashes the record and generates a QR code per lot, so the label on a package points at something checkable rather than a claim printed on the box.

This is Michigan METRC today, not every state's system — the sync is real, not a demo screenshot, and we're not pretending it covers more ground than it does.

reddit.title: How are you tracking chain-of-custody for cannabis batches beyond METRC's own manifest?
reddit.body:
I work on StrainChain, a cannabis-provenance tool built alongside a Michigan METRC integration — it pulls transfer manifests from the state's seed-to-sale API directly (with retry/fallback), rather than someone re-keying a manifest into a spreadsheet after the fact.

Alongside that, every batch gets its own event ledger — cultivated, harvested, lab-tested, packaged, transferred, received at the dispensary — as separate, ordered records rather than one end-of-chain attestation. Batch registration hashes the record and generates a QR code per lot, so what's printed on the package points at something checkable.

Right now this is Michigan METRC specifically — I haven't built out other states' systems yet, and I don't want to imply otherwise.

Curious how others here currently reconcile METRC manifests with their own internal batch records — is a second ledger even useful, or does it just create two sources of truth to keep in sync?

https://strainchain.io/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=strainchain-chain-of-custody&utm_content=a

Disclosure: I work on this project.
